title: Positive-dimensional finitely generated domains have infinitely many maximal ideals
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] that is an integral domain (a commutative ring with no zero divisors). If the Krull dimension of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] is positive, then $A$ has infinitely many maximal ideals.

source.place: the affine positive-dimension argument used with Tags 00G1 and 00FV: a finite-type domain with only finitely many maximal ideals is zero-dimensional

proof.text: Assume for contradiction that the set of maximal ideals of A is finite. If A were not a field, every maximal ideal would be nonzero, because a zero maximal ideal would make A a field. Choose a nonzero element x_m in each maximal ideal m. Since A is a domain, the finite product x=product_m x_m is nonzero, while x belongs to every maximal ideal. The Jacobson property of the finite-type k-algebra A, applied to the prime ideal (0), says that (0) is the intersection of all maximal ideals, so x must be zero, a contradiction. (If the finite set were empty, the existing maximal-ideal theorem applied to the proper ideal (0) would produce a maximal ideal, so this case is also impossible.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00G1 (algebra-lemma-finite-type-field-Jacobson) and Theorem 00FV (algebra-theorem-nullstellensatz), affine positive-dimension argument

proof.text: The spectrum of a field has only the zero prime ideal, so it has no nontrivial strict chain of prime ideals and its Krull dimension is zero.
This contradicts the hypothesis that the Krull dimension of A is positive. Hence the maximal ideals of A are not finite in number, and therefore A has infinitely many maximal ideals.
